title: Synthesis, Structure, and Magnetic Properties of a Large Lanthanide–Transition-Metal Single-Molecule Magnet

material_class.structural_family: Dy6 hexagonal ring capped by two MnIII2MnIV trimers (metallacrown-related)

synthesis.procedure: Complex 1 was prepared by reaction of Dy(NO3)3·5H2O (0.125 mmol), Mn(O2CCH3)2·4H2O (1 mmol), and salicylhydroxamic acid (1 mmol) in wet methanol (30 mL). The mixture was stirred overnight, giving a brown solution and white precipitate. The precipitate was filtered and the brown filtrate was allowed to slowly evaporate. Within three weeks, X-ray quality brown needle crystals of 1 were obtained.
synthesis.time: stirred overnight; crystals within three weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirring in methanol followed by filtration and slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: White precipitate filtered; brown filtrate slowly evaporated to give brown needle crystals of 1.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility shows χT decreasing from 105 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K to 47.4 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with dominant intramolecular antiferromagnetic exchange and/or depopulation of Dy single-ion sublevels. Variable-field magnetization (2–10 K, 0.5–14 T) does not saturate and the ground spin state could not be assigned. Ac susceptibility shows a frequency-dependent out-of-phase signal that increases dramatically near 4 K, supporting SMM behavior, but TB < 2 K and no magnetization hysteresis was observed.
